claims.claim_text: The indexed Shepard Morgan is a high-confidence match to the banker who directed R&A/London.
claims.evidence_excerpt: R&A/London opened officially on May 15 under the direction of Shepard Morgan
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A scholarly history of OSS Research and Analysis identifies the distinctively named Shepard Morgan as director of the London outpost when it opened in 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name, direct OSS organizational context, and contemporaneous bank evidence for the same public figure.
claims.temporal_assessment: The scholarly source places Morgan in the OSS/COI London organization beginning in May 1942.
claims.match_notes: No famous-person match was accepted on name alone; the exact name is joined to a specific OSS leadership role and a tightly dated 1941 institutional affiliation.

sources.excerpt_override: R&A/London opened officially on May 15 under the direction of Shepard Morgan

claims.claim_text: Shepard Morgan was a vice-president of Chase National Bank in 1941, his last identified civilian employer before directing R&A/London in 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Shepard Morgan, Vice-President, Chase National Bank
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NBER's 1941 institutional front matter names Morgan as a Chase National Bank vice-president; Katz places him directing R&A/London when it opened in May 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence because the distinctive name and public institutional roles align with the OSS London leadership chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last identified civilian employer before the May 1942 OSS/COI London role; the sources do not explicitly state that he left Chase to join OSS.
claims.match_notes: Chase is presented as the last identified civilian employer rather than an explicitly documented immediate predecessor. Morgan's separate NBER treasurer role remains an institutional office and is not conflated with bank employment.
